title: Existence of the counit section homotopy
statement:
theorem exists_section_map_with_counit_homotopy {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    {F : X.Modules} (I : InjectiveResolution F)
    (J : InjectiveResolution ((pushforward f).obj F)) (K : CochainComplex Y.Modules ℕ)
    (l : ((pushforward f).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex ⟶ K)
    (hl : QuasiIso l) (β : J.cocomplex ⟶ K)
    (hβ : J.ι.f 0 ≫ β.f 0 = (pushforward f).map (I.ι.f 0) ≫ l.f 0)
    (a : ((moduleSections X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex ≅
      ((moduleSections Y).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).obj
        (((pushforward f).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex))
    (ha : ∀ n : ℕ, a.inv.f n = (presheaf (I.cocomplex.X n)).map
      (eqToHom (by simp) : (⊤ : X.Opens) ⟶ f ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : Y.Opens)).op) :
    ∃ q : ((moduleSections Y).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).obj K ⟶
        ((abelianSections X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).obj
          (standardAbelianResolution X F).cocomplex,
      Nonempty (Homotopy
        (((moduleSections Y).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).map β ≫ q)
        (counitSectionMap f F J))

proof.text: Let T_X and T_Y forget module structures and let R be the standard abelian injective resolution. Abelian direct image G preserves injective objects because it is right adjoint to the exact inverse-image functor. Thus G(R) is a nonnegative complex of injectives. Forgetting preserves the quasi-isomorphism l. Extend by zero to integer degrees; the target is K-injective. The K-injective comparison principle gives a map k:T_Y(K)→G(R) and a homotopy T_Y(l)k∼G(forgottenResolutionMap X I). Restrict the representative and homotopy back to natural degrees. This uses the already proved precomp_bijective_of_quasiIso, not a mapping cylinder.

Let d be the direct image of the forgotten augmentation of I, with the canonical single-complex comparison. The augmentation condition hβ, evaluated in degree zero, gives forgottenAugmentation(Y,J)T_Y(β)=dT_Y(l); all other source degrees are zero. The descOfQuasiIso augmentation equations for forgottenResolutionMap and counitResolutionLift, naturality of the adjunction unit, and the identity unit followed by G(coeff(f,id))=id give forgottenAugmentation(Y,J)counitResolutionAdjoint=dG(forgottenResolutionMap). Precompose the lifting homotopy with d and use these two equalities.

The forgotten augmentation of J is a quasi-isomorphism, and G(R) has injective terms. Apply injectivity of precomposition on homotopy classes (after extension by zero and then restriction) to deduce T_Y(β)k∼counitResolutionAdjoint. Set q to be abelian sections of k followed by abelianPushforwardSectionsIso. Apply sections to the homotopy and postcompose with this isomorphism. Functoriality and the definition of counitSectionMap give Γ(β)q∼counitSectionMap. No comparison a is needed for this first homotopy.

proof_origin.place: K-injective comparison principle, implemented by the existing Sheaf.Algebra.Homology.KInjectiveComparisonPrinciple; augmentation equations and adjunction unit naturality
